author: Maharshi Vyasa (Traditional Translation)
chapter: Chapter 229: Svapna-adhyāya (Rules Relating to the Prognostication of Dreams)
text: Pushkara said: I will now describe the rules relating to the prognostication of dreams (Svapna-adhyaya) to you, O Rama. Dreams dreamt during the first watch (Prahara) of the night bear fruit within a year; those dreamt during the second watch bear fruit within six months; those in the third watch within three months; those dreamt in the fourth watch (early dawn) bear fruit within half a month (fifteen days); and dreams seen at day-break (Brahma-muhurta) bear fruit immediately within ten days. If a person sees an auspicious dream and does not sleep again, that dream bears great fruit.

author: Maharshi Vyasa (Traditional Translation)
text: Auspicious dreams (Shubha Svapna): Climbing a lofty mountain, a palace, a temple, or riding an elephant, a white horse, or a bull indicates victory, prosperity, and royal favor. Crossing a river, ocean, or flooded stream and successfully reaching the shore signifies overcoming obstacles. Seeing white flowers, white garlands, white clothing, sandalwood paste, or bright lamps (Deepam) brings auspicious renown and wealth. Seeing trees blooming with white blossoms, especially in the sky or celestial heights, portends fame and honor.

author: Maharshi Vyasa (Traditional Translation)
text: Inauspicious dreams (Ashubha Svapna): Falling from a high precipice, riding a donkey, camel, or wild boar, or being smeared with dirty mud or thick oil indicates impending sorrow, loss of wealth, or disease. Breaking a bronze or earthen vessel on one's head, losing teeth, or shaving the head completely portends bereavement or grief. Eating bird meat or entering a dark cavern warns of adversity. When an inauspicious dream occurs, the dreamer must not speak of it, but should immediately wash, worship Vishnu, Shiva, or Surya, recite the sacred Gayatri mantra, perform oblations (Homa), and offer gifts to wise elders to nullify the inauspicious effect (Svapna Shanti).

author: Maharshi Vyasa (Traditional Translation)
text: Seeing grass or trees sprouting from one's navel in a dream is highly auspicious, indicating offspring and enduring prosperity; however, vegetation growing from any other part of the body is inauspicious. Seeing oneself possessed of multiple heads or radiant arms signifies elevated authority, spiritual merit, and command over adversaries. Drinking sweet milk, curds, or eating rice pudding (Payasam) indicates good health and blessing from ancestors and deities.
